thought.text: Authentication works — with the admin cookie, the full Blazor UI shell renders. The "nothing at this address" at `/app` suggests routing needs a trailing path. Let me check.

reasoning_content:
Authentication is working — with the admin cookie, the full UI shell is rendered (the navbar "Bovis Bohrsäulenvisualisierung", sidebar containing Home/Konfiguration/Hilfe Symbole, "Admin" displayed in the top bar). The message "Sorry, there's nothing at this address" is because the `PublicBaseUrl` is `/app` — that is, the app treats `/app` as a base-path prefix, and the root page within that base is served at `/app` + `/` = `/app/`? Actually, it's showing "nothing at this address" at `/app`. Hmm, wait — earlier, without the cookie, `/app` displayed "Diese Seite kann nur mit Administrationsrechten aufgerufen werden" (this page can only be accessed with admin privileges). With the cookie, the page renders the shell, but the article shows "Sorry, there's nothing at this address."

This is probably because the root route `/` is within the base path — the app is served at the base `/app`, so the actual home is at `http://localhost:5195/app/` (trailing slash)? Let me try `/app/` with the cookie. Also, the earlier curl to `/` returned 200 and HTML — let me check what `/` displays with the cookie. The base href is "/", but PublicBaseUrl is /app... The message "Serving public files from /app" suggests that the base path is /app. The nav links are relative (href="", "configuration", "help/symbols"), so the home is probably at /app itself... but it says "nothing at this address."

Hmm, the route might be mapped with a route prefix. Let me check Program.cs to understand the routing, and try /app/ with the trailing slash.

action.command: cd /workspace/src/Bovis.Web && COOKIE=UIH234dcbjn0934723dwmZSIZL2342423KUOWidsqw6123e; for p in "app/" "app/index" "app/edit_html?sid=new" "app/configuration" "app/help/symbols"; do echo "=== GET /$p ==="; curl -s -o /tmp/p.html -w "HTTP %{http_code}\n" -H "Cookie: bovis_auth_cookie=$COOKIE" "http://localhost:5195/$p"; grep -o -E "(Liste der Dienste|Administrationsrechten|nothing at this address|Konfiguration|Hilfe|Edit)" /tmp/p.html | sort -u | head -5; done
